outline: 852 Unitary Method for Reverse Percentage Problems

examples.question_text:
A weekly rent is $\$359$ after a $15\%$ increase.
(a) Find the original rent, to the nearest cent.
(b) Explain why taking $15\%$ off $\$359$ does not find the original.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $\$359$ represents $115\%$ of the original.
$\begin{aligned}1\%&=\dfrac{\$359}{115}\\100\%&=\dfrac{\$359}{115}\times100\\100\%&\approx\$312.17\end{aligned}$
(b) The rise was $15\%$ of the original rent, not $15\%$ of the new rent. Taking $15\%$ off $\$359$ gives $\$305.15$, which does not reverse the rise.

examples.question_text: A price is $\$183.70$ after a $17\%$ discount. Find the original price, to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
The sale price is $100\%-17\%=83\%$ of the original.
$\begin{aligned}1\%&=\dfrac{\$183.70}{83}\\100\%&=\dfrac{\$183.70}{83}\times100\\100\%&\approx\$221.33\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Find the original amount in each case.
(a) A price rises by $22\%$. The rise is $\$43.60$. Give the original price to the nearest cent.
(b) A tank loses $7.5\%$ of its water. The amount lost is $45.3$ litres.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The $\$43.60$ is the increase itself, so it represents $22\%$.
$\begin{aligned}1\%&=\dfrac{\$43.60}{22}\\100\%&=\dfrac{\$43.60}{22}\times100\\100\%&\approx\$198.18\end{aligned}$
(b) The $45.3$ litres lost represents $7.5\%$, not $92.5\%$.
$\begin{aligned}1\%&=45.3\div7.5\\1\%&=6.04\text{ litres}\\100\%&=6.04\times100\\100\%&=604\text{ litres}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: $25\%$ of a mass is $68.7$ kg. Use equal quarters to find the full mass.
examples.solution_text:
$25\%=\tfrac14$ of the whole.
Four equal quarters make the full mass.
$68.7\times4=274.8$ kg.

examples.question_text: $18\%$ of a mass is $45$ kg. Use the unitary method to find the full mass.
examples.solution_text:
$45$ kg represents $18\%$ of the full mass.
$\begin{aligned}18\%&=45\text{ kg}\\1\%&=45\div18\\1\%&=2.5\text{ kg}\\100\%&=2.5\times100\\100\%&=250\text{ kg}\end{aligned}$

100 − 17 = 83, so 183.70 represents 83%. The original is 183.70 ÷ 83 × 100 = 221.325301…, giving $221.33. Formatting preserves the baseline mathematics.

The increase itself represents 22%: 43.60 ÷ 22 × 100 = 198.181818…, giving $198.18. The water lost represents 7.5%: 45.3 ÷ 7.5 = 6.04 litres per 1%; 6.04 × 100 = 604 litres. Both parts preserve the baseline mathematics and use the source's change-amount interpretation.
45 kg represents 18%. Dividing by 18 gives 2.5 kg per 1%; multiplying by 100 gives 250 kg. This adapts the supplied known-share question type using the taught unitary method and different values.
